anatomy.intro: Overlapping leaves build a compact rosette, while a short stem and side offsets support its expansion.

parts.function: A thick leaf stores water and presents a broad surface to light.
parts.label: Fleshy leaf

parts.function: New leaves crowd around the growing center.
parts.label: Rosette center

parts.function: The stem supports successive leaves and becomes exposed as lower leaves age.
parts.label: Short stem

parts.function: A small side rosette can enlarge beside the parent.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: Flower stalks lift pink, red or yellow-toned blooms above the rosettes. Outdoors, Echeveria flowers attract bumblebees and hummingbirds, giving these low-growing plants a role beyond their sculptural foliage.

growth.note: Offsets enlarge beside the parent rosette, gradually filling more of the planter.

stages.text: New leaves fill the center while older leaves sit farther out.
stages.title: Compact rosette

stages.text: Lower-leaf loss can reveal a stem; side rosettes may expand.
stages.title: Stem and offsets

stages.text: A sufficiently mature rosette may send a flower stalk above its leaves.
stages.title: Flowering plant

habitat.text: Echeveria is an American genus extending from southwestern Texas to northwestern Argentina. Its succulent leaves form rosettes in a wide range of shapes and colors, with many garden hybrids adding to that diversity. The pale group here has the compact, overlapping leaves typical of the genus.

lookalikes.name: Coppertone-type sedum
lookalikes.text: The sedum has narrower leaves on extending stems, contrasting with these broad, powdery leaves in a compact rosette.

mature.text: A rosette may develop a visible stem and basal offsets as it ages. NC State gives a broad genus range up to about 12 inches tall and wide; individual species and hybrids vary considerably.

milestones.text: Acquired in the Smart Planet Home mixed succulent garden from Home Depot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: The rosettes, copper-toned shoots and broad paddles stayed together in the terra-cotta planter.
milestones.title: Repotted together

milestones.text: A close photograph recorded the powdery rosettes, patchy coating loss and older leaf damage.
milestones.title: Close view recorded

nameStory.text: The genus honors botanical illustrator Atanasio Echeverría y Godoy, a fitting namesake for these sculptural rosettes.
